title: Globalisation & the Digital Social World
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Globalisation & the Digital Social World in A-Level Sociology.

final_note: You worked through the key terms in Globalisation & the Digital Social World.

concepts.def: The increasing interconnection of societies through trade, technology, media and migration, so events and cultures across the world influence one another.
Harvey's idea that modern communication and transport make distant places feel closer, allowing near-instant global connection and exchange.
McLuhan's term for a world drawn together by electronic media, where information spreads instantly and people share a common media culture.
The gap between those with effective access to digital technology and the internet and those without, often along class, age or global lines.
The idea that globalisation spreads a similar consumer culture worldwide, sometimes called Westernisation or McDonaldisation, reducing local diversity.
Castells' idea that social and economic life is increasingly organised around digital information networks rather than fixed physical places.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Globalisation & the Digital Social World — a core area of A-Level Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Globalisation & the Digital Social World brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Globalisation & the Digital Social World.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Harvey's 'time-space compression' describes how technology makes distant places feel:
options: Farther apart
Closer and more connected
Identical in climate
Impossible to reach

mcqs.q: The 'digital divide' is the gap between people who:
options: Like and dislike phones
Do and do not have effective internet access
Are old and young only
Live only in cities
Increases local diversity
Spreads a similar global consumer culture
Ends all media
Has no cultural effect

mcqs.q: Does globalisation only mean economic trade?
options: Globalisation is purely about money and trade.
No - it also involves cultural, political and digital interconnection.
It means everyone now has equal internet access.
It only affects wealthy countries.
The inequality between those with and without effective digital access.
It means everyone now has equal internet access.
It only affects wealthy countries.
It is just people who dislike technology.

mcqs.q: Does cultural globalisation make all cultures identical?
options: Not entirely - shared culture spreads, but local cultures also adapt and resist (glocalisation).
It only affects wealthy countries.
Globalisation has no cultural effect at all.
Every culture becomes exactly the same.
